South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 77 years
ADMISSION DATE: 11/22/24 ADMITTED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Increased fatigue and shortness of breath.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax is a 77-year-old male with a past medical history significant for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), hypertension, and osteoarthritis, who presents to the emergency department with complaints of increased fatigue and shortness of breath over the past week. He reports that his usual activities, including woodworking and light carpentry, have become increasingly difficult due to his symptoms.
He states that he has been experiencing a persistent cough productive of yellow sputum and occasional wheezing, particularly at night. He has been using his albuterol inhaler more frequently, approximately 4-5 times a day. There has been no hemoptysis, but he notes increased swelling in his lower extremities, which he attributes to prolonged sitting while working on his projects.
Mr. Fairfax has a history of smoking, having quit 15 years ago after a 40-pack-year history. He denies any recent travel or sick contacts. His last pulmonary function test was performed in April 2024, showing moderate obstructive lung disease.
He lives alone in and has a supportive family nearby, including a daughter who assists him with transportation. He is currently retired but continues to engage in carpentry as a hobby.
He denies any significant changes in appetite or weight loss but mentions difficulty sleeping due to breathlessness.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + cough, + sputum production, + wheezing, + dyspnea on exertion, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON ADMISSION
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily 4. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 84, BP 130/78, RR 22, O2 sat 92% on room air
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, wheezing noted on expiration, crackles in the bases. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 2+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.2, Hgb 13.5, Hct 40.1, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 138, K 4.0, Cl 102, CO2 28, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, Glucose 102 3. BNP: 550 (elevated) 4. CXR: Hyperinflation of lungs with increased interstitial markings.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD exacerbation: Initiate treatment with systemic corticosteroids (prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days) and continue bronchodilator therapy. Monitor O2 saturation and consider supplemental oxygen if needed. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Monitor blood pressure closely during hospitalization. 3. Lower extremity edema: Elevate legs and monitor for signs of deep vein thrombosis. Consider diuretics if edema worsens. 4. Follow up with pulmonary medicine for outpatient management after discharge.
Patient education provided regarding COPD management, inhaler technique, and the importance of follow-up appointments.
